title: FSSAI — Structure, Functions and Responsibilities
shortDescription: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India: constitution, powers, schemes and what it does on the ground.
genZNote: FSSAI is the main character: it writes the rules, hands out the licences and drops the 'Sahi Bhojan, Behtar Jeevan' slogan. Lock in its who/what/when.

sections.heading: Establishment and Constitution
sections.body: FSSAI was established under Section 4 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (the Authority was set up in 2008; the Act and 2011 Regulations became operational in August 2011). It is administered by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare with headquarters in New Delhi and regional offices across the country. The Food Authority consists of a Chairperson and twenty-two members (one-third women), supported by a Chief Executive Officer (CEO), a Central Advisory Committee and Scientific Panels and the Scientific Committee.

sections.heading: Core Functions and Duties
bullets: Frame Regulations laying down standards and guidelines for articles of food and specify enforcement procedures (Section 16).
Lay down guidelines for accreditation of certification bodies and laboratories, and recognise labs and referral labs.
Provide scientific advice and technical support to Government, collect and collate data on consumption, contamination, residues and emerging risks.
Create an information network, promote general awareness, and contribute to international technical standards (Codex).
Licensing and registration framework for food business operators (FBOs); import clearance of food through authorised officers at ports.
Training programmes such as FoSTaC (Food Safety Training and Certification).

table.caption: FSSAI programmes
rows: Movement for safe, healthy and sustainable food: "Sahi Bhojan, Behtar Jeevan"
Mandatory-trained Food Safety Supervisors in licensed FBOs
Mobile testing labs for on-the-spot screening and awareness
Hygiene Rating / Eat Right Station, Campus, School
Third-party audited recognition of hygienic food outlets and institutions
Organic food mark under the Organic Food Regulations, 2017
Identifier for fortified staples (rice, wheat flour, oil, milk, salt)
Repurpose Used Cooking Oil into biodiesel — limit total polar compounds (TPC) 25%
Food Safety Connect / Food Safety Mitra
Consumer complaint/engagement platforms and training volunteers

sections.heading: Licensing and Registration (threshold logic)
sections.body: Under the FSS (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, petty operators with turnover up to ₹12 lakh register; businesses above that need a State Licence up to ₹20 crore turnover (subject to capacity criteria), and a Central Licence above that or for categories such as importers, central-government premises and certain large manufacturers. Every FBO must display the 14-digit licence/registration number on invoices and labels. Regulatory details change by notification; treat figures here as exam-standard knowledge and confirm against the current FSSAI/Gazette text before relying on them professionally.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: FSSAI is the statutory apex body under the FSS Act, 2006 that frames food standards, regulates manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import of food, and promotes safe and wholesome food.
keyFacts: Section 4 of FSS Act, 2006; HQ New Delhi; under MoHFW.
Food Authority: Chairperson + 22 members; executive head is the CEO.
Eat Right India launched in 2018; slogan "Sahi Bhojan, Behtar Jeevan".
Licence number on label is 14 digits.

highYieldFacts: FSSAI = standard-setter + regulator; enforcement is mostly by State authorities.
Registration up to ₹12 lakh turnover; State licence up to ₹20 crore; Central licence above.
FSSAI is the National Codex Contact Point for India.
commonTraps: Do not say FSSAI itself inspects every shop — State Commissioners/Designated Officers/FSOs do.
Registration ≠ licence: they differ by turnover/capacity.

confusedTerms.distinction: Registration is for petty FBOs (turnover up to ₹12 lakh); licences (State/Central) are for larger operations.

questions.prompt: FSSAI was constituted under which section of the FSS Act, 2006?
questions.explanation: Section 4 provides for establishment of the Food Authority.

questions.prompt: The slogan of the Eat Right India movement is:
questions.explanation: Eat Right India: Sahi Bhojan, Behtar Jeevan.

options: Training and certifying food safety supervisors
questions.explanation: Food Safety Training and Certification trains food handlers/supervisors.

questions.prompt: Who is the executive head of FSSAI?
questions.explanation: The CEO is the chief executive of the Authority.
